info.title: The rvrs node protocol
info.summary: How a node talks to the rvrs API, and how a person's install asks a node for a run.
info.description: README.md in this folder says what the routes are for and what each side does when something gets lost. Fields are only added, and each side ignores what it doesn't know.

servers.description: The rvrs API. RVRS_API points a node at another one.

tags.name: nodes
tags.description: What a node calls about itself.

tags.description: What a person's install calls to run from a node.

post.description: The node trades an enrollment token for a token of its own. Enrolling answers the same every time: under one enrollment token the same key is the same node with the same token, 201 the first time and 200 after that. No enroll revokes or replaces a token, so answers that come late, twice or out of order all say the same thing. Two enrolls with one key at the same moment make one node, and the enrollment token counts it once.

201.description: Enrolled. The node with its token.

200.description: This key enrolled before. The same node with the same token.

401.description: No enrollment token, or one the API doesn't know (UNAUTHORIZED).

403.description: This key belongs to a node that was revoked (NODE_REVOKED).

410.description: The enrollment token expired, was revoked, or has enrolled every node it may and doesn't know this key (ENROLLMENT_CLOSED).

422.description: The body does not match the schema. details.issues names each field and its rule (VALIDATION_ERROR).

429.description: Too many requests. Retry-After says when to try again (RATE_LIMITED).

post.description: The node sends its version, build features, limits and the state of its outbox: when it starts, when one of them changes, and every heartbeatSeconds. Each heartbeat replaces the last, so a retry is safe. dropped counts from the node's start, and boot tells the API when that was.

200.description: Taken. The node and its workspace as the API knows them.

401.description: No credential, or one that is unknown or revoked (UNAUTHORIZED).

403.description: The credential is not a node's (FORBIDDEN), or an admin stopped the workspace's fleet (FLEET_STOPPED).

422.description: The body does not match the schema. details.issues names each field and its rule (VALIDATION_ERROR).

429.description: Too many requests. Retry-After says when to try again (RATE_LIMITED).

get.description: Server-Sent Events over a connection the node opens and holds. hello comes first with the numbers the node works by. work says there is something to claim and nothing about it, and the API writes it again every 15 seconds while a run waits for a node that holds a stream. A comment line every keepAliveSeconds shows the stream is alive. A node is online while it holds this stream, and a new stream with the same token replaces the old one. The event name schedules is reserved.

401.description: No credential, or one that is unknown or revoked (UNAUTHORIZED).

403.description: The credential is not a node's (FORBIDDEN), or an admin stopped the workspace's fleet (FLEET_STOPPED).

429.description: Too many requests. Retry-After says when to try again (RATE_LIMITED).

post.summary: Claim the runs that wait for the node
post.description: The node says every run it holds and how many more it will start. The answer gives it the runs that waited, renews the leases it keeps and says which runs to stop or drop. A run the node holds by the API's count and didn't list is free again at once, so a retry after a lost answer gets that run back as a new attempt. A node claims after every hello and every work, every third of leaseSeconds while it holds a run, and at a random time within claimSeconds while idle. A node sends one claim at a time.

200.description: The runs the node now holds and a verdict for each it listed.

401.description: No credential, or one that is unknown or revoked (UNAUTHORIZED).

403.description: The credential is not a node's (FORBIDDEN), or an admin stopped the workspace's fleet (FLEET_STOPPED).

422.description: The body does not match the schema. details.issues names each field and its rule (VALIDATION_ERROR).

429.description: Too many requests. Retry-After says when to try again (RATE_LIMITED).

post.description: The route every install sends its runs through. A node adds claim for a run that was asked for. The API takes the result when its attempt is the run's newest and the run has no result yet, whether or not the lease ran out in between. A run is told apart by the install and the report's id, so sending it again changes nothing and answers 200. The body may be up to 2 MiB.

200.description: The API had this report already. Nothing changed.

401.description: No credential, or one that is unknown or revoked (UNAUTHORIZED).

403.description: An admin stopped the workspace's fleet (FLEET_STOPPED). The result stays in the outbox.

409.description: A newer attempt has the run, or the run already has its result (CLAIM_LOST). The node drops the result.

422.description: The body does not match the schema. details.issues names each field and its rule (VALIDATION_ERROR).

429.description: Too many requests. Retry-After says when to try again (RATE_LIMITED).

post.summary: Ask a node for a run
post.description: A person's install names a node of its workspace, a tool, a target and options. The answer comes at once with the run's id and the state requested. With a key a retry is safe: the same key from the same install answers 200 with the run it made the first time, and 422 when the rest of the body differs. Without a key a retry asks twice.

200.description: This install asked with this key before. The run as it stands now.

401.description: No credential, or one that is unknown or revoked (UNAUTHORIZED).

403.description: The credential is not a person's install (FORBIDDEN).

404.description: The workspace has no node with this name or id (NODE_NOT_FOUND).

422.description: The body does not match the schema. details.issues names each field and its rule (VALIDATION_ERROR).

429.description: Too many requests. Retry-After says when to try again (RATE_LIMITED).

get.description: The run that was asked for, with its state, and its report once it ended. With wait the answer comes when the state changes or after that many seconds, whichever is first. Safe to repeat.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: How many seconds to hold the answer for a change of state. 0 when left out.

401.description: No credential, or one that is unknown or revoked (UNAUTHORIZED).

403.description: The credential is not a person's install (FORBIDDEN).

404.description: The account has no run with this id (RUN_NOT_FOUND).

node.description: A node's own token: one per node, from the web app or from enrolling.

enrollment.description: An enrollment token. It enrolls a set number of nodes before it expires and does nothing else.

login.description: The token of an install a person signed in, with rvrs login or in the app.

Error.description: The one shape every answer has that is not 2xx.

code.description: What went wrong, as a word to branch on. The list only grows.

details.description: More about the error, when there is more.

requestId.description: Finds the request in the API's logs.

Tags.description: A set of tags: a key and a value each, such as isp=telia, at most 20. A key is a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits, ".", "-" and "_", 63 characters at most. A value is the same, and may start with a digit.

Location.description: Where a node is. The coordinates are decimal degrees. The API rounds them to the precision before it stores them, so a node may send more digits than the precision keeps.

lat.description: Degrees north. The API rounds it to the precision before it stores it.

lon.description: Degrees east. The API rounds it to the precision before it stores it.

place.description: A place as a person would say it, such as Esbjerg, DK.

precision.description: How many digits of the coordinates are kept: exact (4 decimals, about 10 m), area (2 decimals, about 1 km) or city (1 decimal, about 10 km), city when left out. A reader that doesn't know the word treats it as city, the coarsest.

Node.description: A node and the workspace it belongs to, as the API knows them.

id.description: It never changes, whatever the node is called.

name.description: Unique in the workspace, and what --node takes: 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, ".", "-" and "_".

NewNode.description: A node that enrolled, with its token.

id.description: It never changes, whatever the node is called.

name.description: Unique in the workspace, and what --node takes: 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, ".", "-" and "_".

token.description: The node's own token. The same key gets the same token every time, so an answer that comes late or twice says nothing new.

EnrollInput.description: What a node sends to enroll.

key.description: A random word of 128 bits or more that the node makes once, from the system's random source, and keeps. Under one enrollment token the same key is the same node and gets the same token.

name.description: The name the node proposes, its hostname unless it was given one. The API makes the node's name from it.

tags.description: Every tag the node declares, sent whole each time. Left out, the API changes nothing. {} says the node declares none. A tag a person set on the web is never undone by a declaration: a tag is the declaration with the web's edits applied. It counts only when the enroll makes the node. The heartbeat speaks for the node from then on.

location.description: Where the node says it is, sent whole each time. Left out, the API changes nothing. A location a person set on the web is never undone by a declaration. It counts only when the enroll makes the node. The heartbeat speaks for the node from then on.

HeartbeatInput.description: What a node says about itself. It carries no credential, no target and nothing from a report.

protocol.description: The revision of this protocol the node knows, 1 today and 1 when left out. A verdict or an event the node has to act on raises it, and the API sends a node none its revision lacks.

boot.description: A random word the node makes each time it starts, so the API sees a restart.

features.description: The build features the node has: traceroute, ping, mtr, dns, bgp, iperf3, tcp (the TCP probe), mtu (the path MTU check), console. A reader keeps one it doesn't know.

limits.description: What the node allows itself, whatever it is asked. Each one is optional.

waiting.description: Finished runs the API hasn't answered for yet.

dropped.description: Runs given up since this start, because the outbox was full, a run waited too long or the API refused it.

keeps.description: disk or memory. An outbox in memory is lost in a reboot.

tags.description: Every tag the node declares, sent whole each time. Left out, the API changes nothing. {} says the node declares none. A tag a person set on the web is never undone by a declaration: a tag is the declaration with the web's edits applied.

location.description: Where the node says it is, sent whole each time. Left out, the API changes nothing. A location a person set on the web is never undone by a declaration.

Hello.description: The data of the hello event: the numbers the node works by on this stream.

keepAliveSeconds.description: The API writes a comment line this often. A stream silent for twice as long is dead.

claimSeconds.description: The longest a node with nothing to do goes without claiming. Each time it picks a random wait between half of this and all of it. No run depends on this claim: the API repeats work every 15 seconds while a run waits.

heartbeatSeconds.description: How often a node sends a heartbeat when nothing about it changed.

reconnectSeconds.description: After a stream ends, a node waits a random time up to this before it opens a new one. Every failure in a row doubles it, up to 300.

Work.description: The data of the work event. It is empty: the event says there is work, and the claim says what.

attempt.description: Which claim of the run this is, from 1.

Held.description: A run the node holds under one attempt.

ClaimInput.description: What a node sends to claim.

room.description: How many more runs the node will start now, within its own limits.

holding.description: Every run the node claimed and the API hasn't answered a result for: the ones still probing and the ones whose result waits in the outbox. A run the node leaves out is free to be claimed again at once.

RunOptions.description: What the person set. An option left out takes the tool's default. A node refuses a run with an option it doesn't know.

family.description: IPv4 or IPv6. Traceroute, ping and MTR.

rounds.description: Rounds to send. Traceroute and MTR.

intervalMilliseconds.description: The time between packets or rounds. Ping and MTR.

waitMilliseconds.description: The wait for a reply. Traceroute, ping and MTR.

maxHops.description: The last hop to probe. Traceroute and MTR.

firstHop.description: The first hop to probe. Traceroute and MTR.

probe.description: Probes that are not ICMP echo. Traceroute.

mtu.description: true finds the path MTU once the trace is done. Traceroute.

lookups.description: false leaves out reverse DNS and network lookups. Traceroute, ping and MTR.

type.description: The record type, A when left out. DNS.

resolver.description: A resolver of the person's own, asked beside the others. DNS.

ClaimedRun.description: A run the node now holds, with what to run.

attempt.description: Which claim of the run this is, from 1.

tool.description: traceroute, ping, mtr, dns, bgp or iperf3: the word a build names the tool by in features.

Verdict.description: What the API says about a run the node listed.

verdict.description: keep: the lease is renewed. stop: a person stopped the run, so the node ends it now and sends what it measured. drop: a newer attempt has the run or the run has its result, so the node stops and sends nothing. A word the node doesn't know is never read as keep: the node stops the run at once, counts its lease as over and sends what it measured with the outcome stopped and an error that names the word.

leaseSeconds.description: How long each run in runs and each keep is the node's from now. The node claims again every third of it while it holds a run.

runs.description: The runs the node holds for the first time, room of them at most, oldest first.

holding.description: A verdict for each run the node listed.

ResultInput.description: A finished run. Who made it is the API's to say: it stores the run under the node it authenticated and writes that node into the stored report's origin, as the kind node, the node's id and the name the API has for it. A report that says otherwise is stored as this node's all the same, and one whose origin.nodeId names another node is answered 422.

attempt.description: Which claim of the run this is, from 1.

claim.description: The claim a run that was asked for was made under. Left out for a run the node made by itself.

detail.description: The record a product keeps for its own other installs. A node leaves it out.

startedAgoMilliseconds.description: How long before this request the run started, by a clock on the node that only counts forward. The API works out observedStartedAt from it. A node that restarted since the run leaves it out.

id.description: The run's id in the account. For a run that was asked for, it is the id the asker holds.

RunRequestInput.description: What a person's install sends to ask a node for a run.

node.description: The node's name or its id.

tool.description: traceroute, ping, mtr, dns, bgp or iperf3.

expiresIn.description: How many seconds the request may wait for the node. 300 when left out. A lost wake-up is repeated after 15 seconds, so 30 is the least.

key.description: A word the install makes for this request. The same key from the same install answers with the run it made the first time.

RunRequest.description: A run that was asked of a node, and where it stands. Every time but the report's own is the API's clock.

id.description: The run's id, from the moment it was asked for.

state.description: requested, running, ended or expired. A reader keeps a word it doesn't know, shows it and assumes nothing from it.

reason.description: Why an expired run expired: unclaimed when no node ever took it, abandoned when one did and sent no result. null otherwise.

online.description: true while the node holds its event stream.

lastSeenAt.description: When the API last heard from the node. null for a node that never called.

requestedAt.description: When the install asked, by the API's clock.

expiresAt.description: Until when the API gives the run out. A node that holds it may finish later.

attempt.description: How many times the run was claimed. 0 before the first claim.

claimedAt.description: When the newest attempt was claimed, by the API's clock. null before the first claim.

receivedAt.description: When the API stored the result, by the API's clock. null until the run ended.

observedStartedAt.description: When the run started, by the API's clock: receivedAt minus what the node sent as startedAgoMilliseconds. null when the node didn't say. The report's startedAt is the node's own clock, which can be wrong.

report.description: The report, once the run ended. null until then.
